examples.problem: Consider the straight line that passes through $P(1,2,0)$ and parallel to $\mathbf{v}= \langle -4,1,1 \rangle.$ Find all the possible points $A$ on that line such that $PA=6\sqrt{2}.$
examples.worked_solution:
First, we find the vector equation of the line, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}r & =p+tv \\ r & =⟨1,2,0⟩+t⟨-4,1,1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

where $t \in (-\infty, \infty).$

Since $A$ lies on the line, we know that there must be a real number $t$ such that

$$
\overrightarrow{OA} = \langle 1, 2, 0 \rangle + t \langle -4, 1, 1 \rangle
$$

and

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{PA} & =\overset{\to }{OA}-\overset{\to }{OP} \\  & =(⟨1,2,0⟩+t⟨-4,1,1⟩)-⟨1,2,0⟩ \\  & =t\,⟨-4,\,1,\,1⟩ \\  & =⟨-4t,\,t,\,t⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Using the fact that $PA=6\sqrt{2},$ we get:

$$
\begin{aligned}PA & =6\sqrt{2} \\ |\overset{\to }{PA}| & =6\sqrt{2} \\ |⟨-4t,\,t,\,t⟩| & =6\sqrt{2} \\ \sqrt{(-4t)^{2}+{t}^{2}+{t}^{2}} & =6\sqrt{2} \\ \sqrt{18{t}^{2}} & =6\sqrt{2} \\ \pm 3t\sqrt{2} & =6\sqrt{2} \\ t & =\pm 2\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, putting the values $t=\pm 2$ into the equation for the line, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned} & \overset{\to }{O{A}_{1}}=⟨1,2,0⟩+2⟨-4,1,1⟩=⟨-7,4,2⟩, \\  & \overset{\to }{O{A}_{2}}=⟨1,2,0⟩-2⟨-4,1,1⟩=⟨9,0,-2⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the points are $A_1(-7, 4, 2)$ and $A_2(9, 0, -2).$

feedback.problem: Find a vector equation of the line that passes through the points $K(-4,-3,-1)$ and $L(1,2,4).$
feedback.worked_solution:
The vector equation of the straight line passing through $K$ and parallel to $v$ is given by

$$
r=k+tv,
$$

where $t\in (-\infty ,\infty )$ and $k$ is the position vector of $K.$ 

We can find a direction vector by computing the displacement vector between the given points $K(-4,-3,-1)$ and $L(1,2,4),$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =\overset{\to }{KL} \\  & =⟨1,2,4⟩-⟨-4,-3,-1⟩ \\  & =⟨5,5,5⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the vector equation of the line is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}r & =[\begin{aligned}-4 \\ -3 \\ -1\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 5 \\ 5\end{aligned}],\,t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).\end{aligned}
$$
